# Recreation Prompt

Recreate a portrait-first browser zombie shooter called **Zombie Shooter: Pog Dash Afterhours**. Preserve the protected mechanics of the source: the player starts from an overlay, taps/clicks a canvas coordinate to shoot one closest projected zombie, zombies spawn on a timer and advance by perspective depth, holding a large RUN button or using motion energy creates retreat speed, each kill adds one score point, each close contact removes 20 health, and zero health opens a final-score retry overlay. Transform the presentation into a satirical neon-noir after-work leaderboard arcade inspired by Sonic sprint energy and shonen speed lines. Use procedural CSS/canvas visuals: animated neon grid city, skyline, scanlines, acid-green leaderboard score, Chad Shield health bar, bottom-right neon blaster with recoil, glowing office-undead runners, meme callouts like poggers/chad, and mobile-readable CTAs for iOS/Android portrait ratios.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Current implemented game identity
- genre: mobile arcade zombie shooter / survival camera-fallback game.
- objective: tap approaching zombies to remove them, increase score, and survive as long as possible.
- input model: primary tap/click on playfield to shoot one target; hold RUN button or device motion to create retreat speed.
- core loop: start game, spawn zombies at timed intervals, zombies advance through perspective depth, player shoots or runs, score rises on kills, spawn interval tightens as score rises.
- fail/friction state: each zombie reaching close range removes 20 health; at zero health the game stops and shows final score/retry.

## Protected mechanics
- Tap/click is a point-shot against the closest eligible zombie hitbox and removes at most one target per shot.
- Zombies spawn over time, begin far away, advance toward the player, and are sorted by depth for drawing and hit priority.
- Holding RUN or earning motion energy applies retreat speed that pushes effective enemy movement backward without changing scoring.
- Score increments by one per defeated zombie; health starts at 100 and loses 20 per close-contact bite.
- Game states remain start, active play, game over, and restart.
- Difficulty increases by shortening spawn interval as score increases, with a 500ms floor.

## Remixed target
Zombie Shooter: Pog Dash Afterhours reframes the same loop as a satirical neon-noir survival shooter after work: the player is a leaderboard-grinding blaster with a Chad Shield, zombies are meme-office undead runners, score is leaderboard KOs, RUN is a Sonic-like sprint/kite action, and the authored scene is a procedural neon city speed tunnel tuned for portrait one-thumb play.
